title: Paste Special: values and transpose
explanation: A sandwich chain tracks this week's sales by store. Revenue in column D is worked out with formulas. The manager wants a **snapshot** of this week's revenue that won't change when next week's numbers are typed in. Normal copy and paste can't do that, but **Paste Special** can.

tasks.prompt: Click D2 and look at the formula bar. Revenue is a formula, not a typed number.
Copy D2:D6 and paste it normally into F2:F6. Something will go wrong. Look at the results!
tasks.teach: Normal paste copies the **formula**, not the number. Remember, references are relative, so the formula shifts to its new spot.
hints: Select D2:D6, copy, click F2, paste.
You'll get zeros. That's expected this time!

tasks.prompt: Click F2 and look at its formula.
tasks.teach: F2 says `=D2*E2`. The formula moved 2 columns right, so it now multiplies D2 by the empty E2, which gives 0. To copy just the **numbers**, you need Paste Special.

tasks.prompt: Copy D2:D6 again, then right-click F2 and choose Paste Special, then Values. Now F2:F6 holds plain numbers.
tasks.teach: **Paste Special → Values** pastes only what the cells **show**, not the formulas behind them. Use it to freeze a result, or to send numbers to someone without your formulas.
hints: Copy D2:D6, right-click F2, find Paste Special, then pick Values.
Click F2 afterwards: the formula bar should show a number, not a formula.
tasks.answer: Copy D2:D6, right-click F2, Paste Special → Values

tasks.prompt: Next week starts: Downtown sold 150 units. Change B2 to 150. D2 updates, but your snapshot in F2 keeps last week's number.
Last one: the manager wants the store names going across a row instead of down. Copy A1:A6, right-click H1, and choose Paste Special, then Transpose.
tasks.teach: **Transpose** flips data: a column becomes a row, and a row becomes a column.
hints: Copy A1:A6, right-click H1, Paste Special, then Transpose.
H1 to M1 should read: Store, Downtown, Campus, Airport, Mall, Station.
tasks.answer: Copy A1:A6, right-click H1, Paste Special → Transpose

recap: Normal paste copies formulas. Paste Special → Values pastes only the numbers, so they never change. Paste Special → Transpose turns a column into a row.
